html:
Greece is a country at the southern tip of the Balkans, with thousands of islands in the Aegean and Ionian seas. The modern state appears on the map from 1880, but it claims the heritage of the ancient Greek city-states and of the Byzantine Empire.

For nearly four centuries the Greek lands were part of the Ottoman Empire. The Greek War of Independence began in 1821, and with help from Britain, France and Russia a small kingdom was recognised in 1830. A Bavarian prince, Otto, became its first king, and Athens its capital in 1834.

Greece then grew in steps:

  • 1864: the Ionian Islands, from Britain.
  • 1881: Thessaly.
  • 1913: Macedonia, Epirus, Crete and many islands, after the Balkan Wars.
  • 1947: the Dodecanese, from Italy.

The dream of taking back Constantinople and the coast of Asia Minor ended in defeat by Turkey in 1922. The population exchange of 1923 sent over a million Greeks from Turkey and some 400,000 Muslims the other way.

Greece was occupied by the Axis in the Second World War and then fought a civil war until 1949. A military junta ruled from 1967 to 1974 and fell after a failed coup in Cyprus. Greece joined the European Community in 1981 and the euro in 2001. From 2009 a debt crisis brought years of cuts and hardship.
